source.citation: Parkhurst, D. L., Appelo, C. A. J. (1999). User's guide to PHREEQC (Version 2): A computer program for speciation, batch-reaction, one-dimensional transport, and inverse geochemical calculations. U.S. Geological Survey Water-Resources Investigations Report 99-4259.

transcription.from: the published report (PDF from pubs.usgs.gov), section Equations for the Newton-Raphson Method, Activity of Water, Eq. 25, p. 17, read on the page image
transcription.note: PHREEQC 3.7.3 computes the activity of water with this coefficient for every database without a Pitzer or SIT block: measured with phreeqc.dat, llnl.dat, wateq4f.dat and minteq.v4.dat in a 2 mol/kg NaCl solution at 25 and 60 C, a_w equals 1 - 0.017 times the sum of the molalities of the solutes to 1e-13.

water_activity_coefficient.description: Coefficient of the approximation of the activity of water based on Raoult's law, a_H2O = 1 - 0.017 sum_i n_i / W_aq, the sum over the aqueous species and W_aq the mass of water in kg.
